newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares open steady, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares open steady, seen firm.

text.p: Russian shares opened unchanged from last week's close on Monday morning and traders said they had modest expectations for growth ahead of the announcement of a presumedly reform-oriented government.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index opened at 328.98 after closing on Friday at 329.37.
Trading volumes were average on the Russian Trading System at 0935 GMT, operators said.

Preferred shares of metals company Norilsk Nickel NKEL_p.RTS ticked up to $4.70 from $4.55 on Friday and oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS rose to $14.42 from $14.30. Energy utility UES EESR.RTS had edged down to $0.2249 from $0.2256.
Traders said there had been no reaction to President Boris Yeltsin's offer of a First Deputy Prime Ministership to Boris Nemtsov, the young reform-minded governor of Nizhny Novgorod.
"There was nothing because Nemtsov's name had been expected in the government, and so far it is just an offer," said Anton Kudryashov, chief equities trader at Renaissance Capital.
"But in general when the cabinet is formed, if there are reformers of that sort, you might expect a short period of growth -- for a few days."

Traders expected the market to be even or slightly up for the day, with best performance among some regional telecoms, and were watching for news of Yeltsin's forthcoming summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helsinki, now scheduled for March 20.
They were also looking for indications about natural monopoly restructuring, which may be a priority in the new cabinet.

Russian investors were expected by some dealers to come back into the market after an easing in T-bill rates towards the end of last week. A back-up in yields last week had sent some banks back to the T-bill market, their traditional investment target.
